To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
firms are motivated to implement green supply chain management practices in response to competitive and stakeholder pressures.

firms are more likely to implement green supply chain management practices when they face pressure from their rivals and stakeholders, especially when they receive top management support for their green initiatives.

(1) Rival pressure and stakeholder pressure influence green supply chain management implementation through the mediation of top management support; and (2) Rival pressure, stakeholder pressure, and top management support influence the implementation of green supply chain management practices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of top managers in the green supply management process and the influence of competitive and stakeholder pressure on the adoption of green supply practices.
the role of rivalry and stakeholders as a driver of green supply management practices and the role of top managers as an important enablers for such practices.
how competitive pressures from rival firms influence firms to implement green practices in the supply chain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the more the top management is supportive towards green supply management, the more firms will be able to implement such practices in their supply chains.
the study results suggest that the role of top-management support for environmental initiatives is a critical element in linking stakeholder and rival pressure to green supply chain practices.

firms with higher levels of rivalry and stakehouseholder pressure are likely to have higher levels of top management support, which in turn will result in higher levels of green supply management practices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the role of top managers is critical to the successful implementation of green supply management practices.
top management support for green supply management is a critical enabler of the relationship between competitive pressure and green supply management practices.
firms that have strong top management support for their environmental initiatives are more likely to respond to the environmental pressures they face from their competitors and stakeholders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the implementation of green supply chain practices is not just a matter of responding to external pressures.
top managers can be instrumental in helping their firms to respond to environmental pressures from stakeholders and competitors by providing the necessary support to implement green supply practices.
the competitive and stakeholder pressures that firms face can be harnessed to pursue environmental initiatives, but only if top management supports these initiatives.
